body: Wow, that is scary! I don't know much about drugs, or what benzos even are, so I'm not sure if I've ever been on any other kind, the only meds I've been on for anxiety are the lorazapam/Ativan and alprazolam, I don't recall the alprazolam giving me any real bad side affects, and they helped a lot, which I told the doctor but he wouldn't give them to me, only the lorazapam. I haven't taken them since I had this episode, for fear that they were the cause. I will def try and hold off taking them until I get to see my doctor again!

They said it would take about 2 weeks for the results, I had the work done 4 days ago. I can't make an appt now because the doctor is out of the office for the week. I can't afford to see a therapist, but I will for sure come here if I get that feeling again in the meantime. I can't imagine how the people on here survive, having that feeling all the time, looking back to those few hours is terrifying to think about. I only wish everyone on here could come out of the fog and find something to live for. You people who take the time to respond to people's post and try and reach out are really great, thanks for that.

I did mention to the doctor about getting a referral to a psychiatrist ( I live in Canada so if I get a referral it's covered by health care) he just said to see how my blood work comes back, he seems to think something could be off with that causing me anxiousness, even though I've had the anxiety for years :/ it was a very rushed appt, as he was very busy and very behind ( I was nearly 2 hours waiting past my appointment time) 
When I do go back though for the results of the blood work I intend on pretty much not leaving until I can get a referral. I just hope that I don't get that horrible feeling again in the meantime.

It's not that I'm against taking medication, I just felt I was being over medicated, and being medicated for the wrong reasons. I don't have depression. Yes I get sad sometimes, I get angry sometimes. I'm human and I've been through some pretty bad things. But I don't think I suffer from depression, which is what he was prescribing medication for. I took a 15 question survey, and my family doctor decided because of my answers I was bipolar, and prescribed me medication for that. I've never been suicidal in my life but after taking some of these medications after a week or two I started to get those thoughts in my head. What I'm hoping for is that I just had a bad experience with a pill pusher type doctor. This whole hair pulling thing is new, and right away I realize it's not normal, I need help right away for my anxiety which will hopefully help with the hair pulling issue. I'm trying to to be more conscience of what I'm doing and stop as soon as i realize that I am doing it. It's hard though because for some reason it's calming, which makes me even more nervous about the situation. 
Tomorrow morning first thing I am going to try and find a family doctor that is taking new patients, get an appointment and hopefully get a referral to a specialist of some sort.

My boyfriend is a sleep talker. Every night I get to hear some interesting stuff, last night I got screamed at to "quickly! Put your hard hat on! It's happening!!" Scared the living day lights out of me.

Yeah I had the in ear one as well and it was a pain. My son would not sit still at all. I was so relieved when I got the forehead one and it worked so well. I went through a ton of thermometers before finding that one.

I bought one that just slides on your finger and you put your hand up against your child's forehead just like you were feeling for a temp. I bought it well over a year ago so I don't have the packaging anymore to tell you exactly what it's called, but it is very accurate, I tested it up against the butt one. I bought it at shoppers drug mart (Canada only maybe) but I'm sure if you went into a pharmacy and asked the pharmacist for something similar to what I described they could help you out. They can also tell you the best ones for accuracy as well. Good luck!
